providers.title: Reductions: composition, computable sets, countability
providers.scope: A reduction is a computably enumerable set of triples (string, argument, value). There is a reduction computing A from A; reductions compose; a set is computable iff it is computable from the empty set; at most countably many sets are computable from a given set.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Automorphisms of the degrees preserve the least degree and joins
providers.scope: An order automorphism of the Turing degrees fixes the degree of the computable sets and satisfies pi(a v b) = pi(a) v pi(b); its inverse is an automorphism.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Uniform computation of a sequence computed step by step
providers.scope: If X_0 is computable from T and each X_(n+1) is computed from X_n + T by one of two fixed reductions, selected by one fixed bit of X_n, then the whole sequence, and the sequence of the selections, is computable from T by one reduction.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Real numbers as cuts
providers.scope: The cut map is one-to-one; the degree of a rational affine combination of reals is at most the join of their degrees; every noncomputable degree is the degree of an irrational number in (0,1).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Baire's theorem in the line and the plane
providers.scope: A nonempty open subset of R or R^2 is not meager; a comeager set is dense.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A Borel function is continuous on a comeager set
providers.scope: For a Borel function from R or R^2 to the Cantor space or to the natural numbers there is a comeager set on which its restriction is continuous.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The least index of a reduction for sums is a Borel function
providers.scope: If F is a Borel function from the reals to sets with F(x+y) computable from F(x) + F(y) for all x, y, then the least index of a reduction computing F(x+y) from F(x) + F(y) is a Borel function of (x,y).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The avoidance lemma
providers.scope: If Y is not computable from A, then the set of pairs (u,v) of reals such that Y is computable from A and the cuts of u and v is meager.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Recovery from four values
providers.scope: Let F be a Borel function from the reals to sets with countable fibres and F(x+y) computable from F(x) + F(y). For an irrational t in (0,1) and all (u,v) in a comeager set there is a rational delta in (0,1) such that the cut of t is computable from F(u) + F(u-v) + F(v-u+delta t) + F(v-u+delta(t-1)).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The bounded walk
providers.scope: The walk s_(n+1) = s_n + delta(t - r_n), with r_n read from one bit of F(u+s_n) that sends the walk inwards near both ends, stays in [b_-, b_+], and s_n = delta(n t - sum of r_k).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: From a Borel representation to a function on the line
providers.scope: If a Borel function Fhat represents an automorphism pi, then F = Fhat o C is Borel on the reals, deg F(x) = pi(d(x)), F has countable fibres, and F(x+y) is computable from F(x) + F(y).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: An automorphism with a Borel representation moves no degree downwards
providers.scope: If an automorphism pi of the Turing degrees is represented by a Borel function, then a <= pi(a) for every degree a. No hypothesis is used.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Rigidity of the Turing degrees
providers.scope: Assume the theorem of Slaman and Woodin that every automorphism of the Turing degrees has a Borel representation (hypothesis (SW), not proved in the course). Then every automorphism of the Turing degrees is the identity.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
